latest_release.name: Google Surf MCP v1.1.6
latest_release.body:
Google Surf MCP 1.1.6 improves Auto Ontology, evidence handling, and optional provider setup.

- Adds query-focused evidence, cached follow-up reads, and explicit requirement/gap receipts. The balanced default is preserved; coherent extraction is opt-in.
- Separates ontology schema terms from instance assertions and adds project-, time-, and unit-aware full-population aggregates.
- Fixes pinned E5 tokenizer discovery and fingerprints embedding/runtime compatibility.
- Isolates source-reading browser traffic with DNS-validated, IP-pinned requests and private-network guards.
- Integrates optional OrcaRouter API-key and PKCE setup with CSRF protection, bounded model discovery, and owner-only credential storage.
- Fixes Windows credential-permission validation and updates the manual repair workflow actions without enabling scheduled Google probes.

The release is checked on Linux and Windows with Node.js 22 and 24. Existing research data is preserved; derived vector indexes may need rebuilding after the runtime fingerprint changes.

Known dependency warning: the stealth dependency chain retains a [low-severity deepmerge advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4) with no upstream patched version. No forced downgrade is applied.

# google-surf-mcp English | [Korean](./README.ko.md) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/google-surf-mcp)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/google-surf-mcp) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/google-surf-mcp)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/google-surf-mcp) [![ci](https://github.com/HarimxChoi/google-surf-mcp/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/HarimxChoi/google-surf-mcp/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![MCP Toplist](https://mcptoplist.com/badge/io.github.HarimxChoi%2Fgoogle-surf-mcp.svg)](https://mcptoplist.com/server/io.github.HarimxChoi%2Fgoogle-surf-mcp) [![google-surf-mcp MCP server](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/HarimxChoi/google-surf-mcp/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/HarimxChoi/google-surf-mcp)

Sponsored by SearchApi

[Install](#quick-start) · [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) · [Architecture](#architecture) · [Tools](#tools) Google Surf MCP searches the web, papers, and codebases, then uses Auto Ontology to organize what you read into a local knowledge graph. Start without an API key or a separate database server, and build a personal knowledge base from connected sources and project records. ## Benchmarks ### Web search vs Google AI Mode Eight developer questions covered Python TaskGroup, SQLite WAL, Kubernetes probes, Fetch, Redis TTL, Docker Compose, PyTorch, and Rust. Examples included SQLite's concurrent-writer limitations and whether PyTorch's `inference_mode()` replaces `model.eval()`. The answer model paired with Google Surf was **[DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1017)](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/updates/)** (`deepseek-flash`, temperature 0, thinking disabled). | Evaluation | Google Surf + DeepSeek | Google AI Mode | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Result | **22/24** | **24/24** | Three required checkpoints per question; the numbers count fully met checkpoints, not whole-answer accuracy. Recorded on 2026-11-07, not a new evaluation of the current release. ### Auto Ontology comparison Both systems built ontologies from 48 revision-pinned model-card and configuration files covering 16 open-weight model releases. Their retrieved evidence was passed to the same DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1017) model (`deepseek-flash`), SQL-generation prompt, and database: **Google Surf 116/120, NVIDIA Auto Ontology 113/120**. This compares ontology-backed retrieval, not the products' default agents. [Evaluation setup, live-ranking results, and resource measurements](./guides/benchmarks.md) ## Architecture ### Technology stack | Layer | Technologies | | --- | --- | | Runtime and protocol | TypeScript, Node.js 22.13+, MCP SDK, Zod | | Browser search | System Chrome, Playwright, shared browser broker and reusable tabs | | Source reading | HTTP, isolated headless BrowserContext, Mozilla Readability, Turndown | | Documents and OCR | LiteParse CPU OCR; optional Xberg for Office; OfficeParser fallback; hwp-convert; pdf-lib; Sharp | | Local storage | SurrealDB with embedded RocksDB, durable catalog and payloads, rebuildable indexes | | Retrieval and ranking | Exact match, BM25, Multilingual E5-small q8/ONNX, HNSW, graph retrieval, RRF, cached E5 reranking | | Code indexing | Tree-sitter for Python, TypeScript, and C++ structure | | Graph analysis | Graphology, PageRank, Louvain communities, provenance and lineage projections | | Network controls | Undici, DNS/IP-pinned reads, SSRF checks, deny-by-default source-reader proxy | OCR is configurable; Xberg does not add another OCR or embedding model. Live-only search uses BM25/RRF without loading E5. [Architecture details](./guides/auto-ontology.md) · [Lightweight configuration](./examples/lightweight-documents.env) ## Quick start Requires Node.js 22.13+ and Chrome or Chromium for browser search. CI covers Node 22 and 24 on Linux and Windows. Register the server in your MCP client: ```json { "mcpServers": { "google-surf": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "google-surf-mcp@latest"] } } } ``` Restart the client. Auto Ontology is enabled by default; the local embedding model may be downloaded when you first index content. For search and extraction without the database or embedding model, set `SURF_RESEARCH=false` in the server environment. [Client setup, local installation, and SearchApi configuration](./guides/getting-started.md) ## Search - Search through system Chrome without an API key - Dedicated logged-out profile; your personal Chrome profile is never read or copied - Multi-strategy SERP parsing with geometric verification - Removal of sponsored results and knowledge panels - CAPTCHA detection and environment-specific recovery - Parser self-healing and context fallback Browser search is the default. [SearchApi](https://www.searchapi.io/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=sponsorship&utm_campaign=google_search_api&utm_content=HarimxChoi_google-surf-mcp) is an optional primary provider or fallback; it requires your own account, key, and credits. ## Supported AI providers and gateways - [OrcaRouter](https://www.orcarouter.ai/ref/ref_7fd137d6c7b30793af2f) (free models available) [Optional LLM-assisted repair and OrcaRouter setup](./guides/configuration.md#orcarouter) ## Tools Seven tools are available with Auto Ontology enabled: | Tool | Use | | --- | --- | | `search` / `search_parallel` | Discover **new web sources** and read them in the same call with `extract_mode`. | | `scholar_search` | Find paper-specific Google Scholar metadata. | | `extract` | Read a web page, PDF, or repository from an **already-known URL**. | | `project_memory_search` | **Local-only** search of indexed project knowledge; no live web search. | | `project_memory` | Manage projects, save research records, index user-approved local folders, and export graphs. | | `health` | Inspect search and local runtime status. | Providing `project_id` to web search does not make it local-only. Use `project_memory_search` for stored knowledge. [Tool parameters, limits, follow-up reads, and repeatable source collection](./guides/tools.md) ## Google Surf Auto Ontology Search and extraction results are saved automatically. Plans, experiments, failures, and decisions are linked when your agent records them through `project_memory`. Search stored knowledge across selected projects with exact-match, keyword, semantic, and graph retrieval, RRF fusion, and a shared reranker. Projects stay separate by default. Selected projects can link knowledge using matching DOIs, repository URLs, or explicitly registered aliases; original records are not merged or moved. Create a standalone graph explorer for one project: ```text project_memory(action="export", project_id="my-project", export_format="html", export_view="graph") ``` The HTML explorer includes PKM, lineage, and ontology views with PNG/JSON downloads. DOT and Neo4j exports are also available. The feature was renamed from Research to Auto Ontology; existing `SURF_RESEARCH*` settings, `project_memory*` tools, CLI names, and storage paths still work. [Ontology, lineage, code indexing, and export details](./guides/auto-ontology.md) ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | | --- | --- | | [Getting started](./guides/getting-started.md) | Installation, clients, browser search, SearchApi setup | | [Tools and workflows](./guides/tools.md) | Tool parameters, limits, evidence responses, source collection | | [Auto Ontology](./guides/auto-ontology.md) | Storage, code structure, graph retrieval, lineage, exports | | [Configuration](./guides/configuration.md) | Environment variables, resource settings, OrcaRouter | | [Operations and security](./guides/operations.md) | CAPTCHA, cache cleanup, CLI, privacy, optional Codex hooks | | [Benchmarks](./guides/benchmarks.md) | Measurements, conditions, and evaluation boundaries | [Contributing](./CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Changelog](./CHANGELOG.md) · [MIT License](./LICENSE)
